<!--
  PMS 1.43.3 GET /library/sections/{key}/all?type=2&unwatched=0 against a SHOW library. Recorded
  2026-08-05 from a real server (plex-safety rule 11). Titles and ids are sanitized; attribute NAMES,
  ordering and the container shape are verbatim.

  NOTE THE QUERY. This is NO LONGER the read Shortlist makes: the show read now sends
  `?type=2&viewedLeafCount!=0`, because `unwatched=0` omits a series whose show-level watch-state row
  was never established (issue #108 — see the correction below and
  `pms_watched_episodes_rollup.xml.txt`). The recording is kept because it is the evidence for that
  change, and because the ROW shapes it captures — viewed/total pairs, a missing `lastViewedAt` — are
  what `_watched_item` must parse either way.

  WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS.

  `pms_watched_incremental.xml.txt` records the same endpoint against a MOVIE library, and until now
  it was the only recording we had. The show case was assumed rather than measured, and the whole
  already-watched rule turns on it — so the assumption was load-bearing and unverified.

  WHAT WAS MEASURED, on a show section, as the admin account:

    ?type=2&unwatched=0   -> every show with viewedLeafCount > 0, INCLUDING barely-started ones.

  The ten rows below are the real viewed/total pairs observed, unchanged:

      2/23   4/142   47/47   14/67   42/122   2/176   4/138   100/100   12/17   4/38

  THE POINT. `unwatched=0` on a show library does NOT mean "fully watched". It returns a series from
  its FIRST episode — 2 of 176 is 1.1% and still comes back. Plex has no show-level `viewCount`; a
  `<Directory>` carries only `viewedLeafCount` and `leafCount`, so every yes/no answer about a show
  is somebody's threshold over those two numbers, and Plex's own threshold is "more than zero".

  This is what settled the 1.2 change to the already-watched rule. Shortlist used to apply its own
  bar on top (>=80% of episodes, or a length-scaled floor of ~3), which meant five of the ten shows
  above — everything under its floor — were still eligible to be recommended back to the person
  watching them. A 0% row now treats started as watched, matching the server. See
  `RowPolicy.zero_pct_exclusions`.

  Note also the mark-as-watched case (ratingKey 5006): a bulk "mark as played" sets the leaf counts
  equal with no per-episode play history, which the playback-history API would never have shown.

  CORRECTION, 2026-09-01 (issue #108), in two parts — the second corrects the first.

  **The column was never recorded.** This fixture's `lastViewedAt` values are invented: the first
  three are copied from `pms_watched_incremental.xml.txt` (a MOVIE library) and the rest are round
  numbers. Only the viewed/total pairs listed above were ever measured. Treat every other value here
  as illustrative.

  **The row that had no `lastViewedAt` was RIGHT, and was wrongly "corrected" away.** A first pass at
  #108 removed it after probing the live server for shows missing that attribute and finding zero of
  534. That probe asked `?type=2&unwatched=0` — the very query that EXCLUDES such shows — so the
  answer could only ever be zero, and it read like proof they do not exist. It is a selection effect,
  not evidence, and it cost a wrong diagnosis. The row is restored below.

  What the same server actually shows when asked properly (`?type=2` unfiltered, plus the episode
  read; see `pms_watched_episodes_rollup.xml.txt`):

    ?type=2&unwatched=0   ->   533 shows
    ?type=2               ->  4880 shows, of which 491 have viewedLeafCount > 0
    ?type=4&unwatched=0   ->  9563 episodes, rolling up to exactly those same 491 shows

  **20 of those 491 never came back from `?type=2&unwatched=0`.** Every one has correct episode
  counts and NO `lastViewedAt` on the show row. So this endpoint filters on the show's own watch-state
  row, not on `viewedLeafCount`, and a show whose row was never established is invisible to it — which
  is what happens when a series or a season is marked watched rather than an episode played. That is
  issue #108, and it is why `watched_titles` now supplements this read with the episode-level one.

  Row 5006 therefore records a show this endpoint would NOT return, and is kept for a narrower reason
  than "the supplement handles it" — it does not: `_shows_from_episodes` builds recovered shows
  directly from a plexapi object and never parses a `<Directory>`. It is here so `_watched_item` is
  proven tolerant of a missing `lastViewedAt`, which the unfiltered `?type=2` genuinely returns.
-->
